frequency_question: How often do such party-priority bills successfully pass the U.S. Senate when the sponsoring party holds sufficient alignment to attempt it?
membership_rule: Includes major partisan electoral reform or integrity bills pushed by the chamber majority or a major unified caucus within a 2-year Congress. Excludes bipartisan consensus packages and routine appropriations.
provenance_note: rate of 0% from only 4 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 4 prominent partisan federal election bill attempts in the Senate examined; 0 passed due to procedural thresholds like the filibuster, though my aperture strictly excludes the procedural friction itself and measures only the underlying will/capability persistence.
known_gaps: Excludes minor or unvoted committee-only variants.
validity_reason: Valid until the end of the current congressional structural baseline.
